Allowed origins are set in **`worker/src/index.ts`**, inside the Hono `cors()` middleware call (`app.use('*', cors({ origin: (origin) => {...} }))`, lines 19–30). Currently it allows:

- `http://localhost:4200` (exact match)
- any origin ending in `.pages.dev`
- any origin ending in `.workers.dev`

Anything else returns `null` (rejected). This logic is documented in `docs\DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` (lines ~88–104) as the fix for Hono's array-based `origin` only doing literal string matches.

**To add a new custom domain**, edit the `origin` function in `worker/src/index.ts` (line 21 area) and extend the condition at line 23–26, e.g.:
```ts
origin === 'http://localhost:4200' ||
origin === 'https://your-custom-domain.com' ||   // add this
origin.endsWith('.pages.dev') ||
origin.endsWith('.workers.dev')
```
No other file needs changes for CORS; this is the single source of truth for allowed origins.
